value.notes: 3CE's own official site confirms it serves San Luis Obispo County, and separately lists Arroyo Grande among its named member communities. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Arroyo Grande/San Luis Obispo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

required_documents.notes: The city's page describes general submittal requirements; a solar-specific checklist distinct from the general construction plan checklist was not confirmed this session.

permit_fees.notes: Plan check fees must be paid prior to the start of plan review, per the city's Comprehensive Fee Schedule (FY 2025-26); specific solar dollar amounts were not confirmed this session.
